survey.scope: Garment reconstruction, assembly, topology, layering, texture, deformation, and dynamic evaluation methods relevant to image2outfit.

inclusionCriteria: Official primary publication page is available.
The method can change a production requirement, implementation experiment, or benchmark in image2outfit.
The publication year matches this annual baseline.
exclusionCriteria: Secondary summaries without a primary publication URL.
Methods with no traceable relevance to garment production or evaluation.

capabilities.description: Editable garment panels, seams, connectivity, and 2D-to-3D correspondence.
Explicit graph-based seam pairing and auditable garment assembly.
Controlled topology adaptation with UV, face orientation, and material continuity.
Declared layer ordering, anchoring, clearance, and penetration severity evaluation.
Multi-view, occlusion-aware, seam-consistent PBR material production.
Garment-appropriate deformation with measured runtime and generalization evidence.
Temporal geometry, collision, identity, and perceptual review beyond static poses.

publications.title: ReWeaver: Towards Simulation-Ready and Topology-Accurate Garment Reconstruction
publications.reportedClaim: Reconstructs panels, seams, connectivity, and 2D/3D correspondence from as few as four RGB views for simulation-ready garments.

publications.title: AutoSew: A Geometric Approach to Stitching Prediction with Graph Neural Networks
publications.reportedClaim: Predicts stitch correspondences from 2D contours using graph matching and differentiable optimal transport, including multi-edge connections.

publications.title: ExMesh: EXplicit Mesh Reconstruction with Topology Adaptation
publications.reportedClaim: Combines explicit mesh optimization with adaptive splitting and merging while maintaining UV coordinates.

publications.title: DAMA: Disentangled Body-Anchored Gaussians for Controllable Multi-Layered Avatars
publications.reportedClaim: Models garment separation, stacking order, penetration rate, and penetration depth for controllable multi-layer avatars.

publications.title: NI-Tex: Non-isometric Image-based Garment Texture Generation
publications.reportedClaim: Generates spatially aligned PBR materials from non-isometric image and geometry pairs using uncertainty-guided multi-view baking.

publications.title: NaTex: Seamless Texture Generation as Latent Color Diffusion
publications.reportedClaim: Generates texture color directly in 3D to address occlusion, boundary alignment, and cross-view consistency limitations.

publications.title: PhySkin: Physics-based Bone-driven Neural Garment Simulation
publications.reportedClaim: Uses reduced-space bone handles and self-supervised physical objectives for fast garment draping with collision avoidance.

publications.title: UNIC: Neural Garment Deformation Field for Real-time Clothed Character Animation
publications.reportedClaim: Learns an instance-specific continuous deformation field for complex garment topology and unseen motion sequences.

publications.title: Human Geometry Distribution for 3D Animation Generation
publications.reportedClaim: Evaluates detailed clothing dynamics using geometric metrics, temporal consistency, and a perceptual user study.

methodAssessments.rationale: Use structured panel and seam representations as the editable canonical source when reconstruction provides them.
implementationImplications: Represent image-derived garments as explicit panels and seam connectivity before final meshing.
Persist both 2D pattern-space and 3D garment-space correspondence when reconstruction is used.
Reject visually similar but unstructured shells as the canonical source when panel topology is recoverable.
rejectionCriteria: No traceable panel or seam model for an image-reconstructed garment.
Topology cannot support controlled edits or simulation-oriented validation.

methodAssessments.rationale: Prototype graph-based seam pairing while retaining an auditable manual fallback until code and model rights are verified.
implementationImplications: Store seam pairing as a graph instead of relying on object names or manual adjacency alone.
Validate edge-length compatibility, orientation, and multi-edge connectivity before cloth assembly.
Keep manual stitching as an auditable fallback until the learned predictor is licensed and reproduced.
rejectionCriteria: Unpaired or ambiguous pattern edges remain in a release candidate.
Stitch topology changes without an explicit connectivity diff.

methodAssessments.rationale: Adopt controlled coarse-to-fine topology refinement with UV and material continuity checks.
implementationImplications: Any topology refinement must preserve UV continuity and material alignment.
Record vertex and face count changes and reject new degenerate or fragmented geometry.
Prefer coarse-to-fine refinement over uniformly dense generation.
rejectionCriteria: Topology edits create degenerate faces, UV discontinuity, or unnecessary density.
High detail is produced only by uncontrolled subdivision.

methodAssessments.rationale: Adopt explicit layer ordering, body anchoring, and penetration severity evidence for layered garments.
implementationImplications: Declare layer order and body anchoring for every garment component.
Measure penetration count and depth, not only render appearance.
Keep body-conforming layers separate from outer loose layers.
rejectionCriteria: Layer order is implicit or inconsistent across poses.
Critical body or inter-garment penetration remains unresolved.

methodAssessments.rationale: Prototype multi-view, uncertainty-aware PBR material generation without treating a single projection as finished texture.
implementationImplications: Generate or author PBR channels separately from geometry.
Bake from multiple views and prioritize uncertain or occluded regions in later passes.
Evaluate seam continuity, cross-view color consistency, and material response.
rejectionCriteria: A single projected image is treated as production-ready texture.
Visible seams, cross-view color drift, or material-channel mismatch remain.

methodAssessments.rationale: Use 3D-consistent color generation as a comparison target for seams, occluded regions, and cross-view consistency.
implementationImplications: Benchmark texture seams and occluded regions against a 3D-consistent representation.
Do not accept multi-view texture baking when hidden regions are unreviewed.
rejectionCriteria: Occluded texture regions are filled without evidence or review.
Boundary alignment fails at UV islands or garment edges.

methodAssessments.rationale: Prototype reduced bone-handle and physics-constrained deformation for loose garments; do not infer production readiness from the preprint alone.
implementationImplications: Treat bone handles as a reduced deformation space rather than assigning arbitrary weights only.
Separate offline physics fitting from runtime handle evaluation.
Benchmark loose garments across body shapes and required poses before runtime adoption.
rejectionCriteria: Loose garments rely only on static linear blend skinning without deformation evidence.
Runtime claims are made without measured cost and pose/body generalization tests.

methodAssessments.rationale: Benchmark garment-specific continuous deformation against bone-driven and physical baselines.
implementationImplications: Use per-garment deformation evaluation when topology is complex.
Benchmark continuous-field deformation against bone-driven and physics baselines.
Do not require one model to generalize across unrelated garments.
rejectionCriteria: A deformation method is selected without a garment-specific benchmark.
Real-time suitability is assumed without target-device measurement.

methodAssessments.rationale: Use both geometric and perceptual temporal evaluation for garments whose quality depends on motion.
implementationImplications: Evaluate deformation with both geometric error and perceptual review.
Test short transitions and long motion consistency instead of isolated poses only.
Preserve garment identity and fine detail across animation.
rejectionCriteria: Only static poses are used to claim dynamic garment quality.
Temporal flicker or identity drift is not reviewed.

productionRequirements.statement: Image-derived garments must have an explicit panel model or an auditable reason for a non-panel construction.
The editable source must preserve the relationship between design references, panels, and the final mesh.
Seam connectivity must be stored explicitly and checked for unmatched, reversed, or incompatible edges.
Assembly changes require a connectivity diff and regenerated pose evidence.
Topology changes must preserve UV continuity, face orientation, and material assignment.
Degenerate faces, fragmented shells, and uncontrolled density are release blockers.
Every component must declare its body or garment layer and intended clearance.
Penetration must be measured across required poses, including depth or severity, not only counted visually.
Textures must be reviewed across all required views with separate material channels where applicable.
Seams, occluded regions, and cross-view color or material consistency must be explicitly inspected.
Tight and loose garments must use different deformation strategies where needed.
Loose garments require a measured bone-handle, physics, or neural deformation benchmark before runtime claims.
Required static poses are necessary but not sufficient for loose or layered garments.
A motion sequence must be reviewed for temporal consistency, collision, detail retention, and customer-visible artifacts.
